title: Reach of 21 CFR Part 208 and who counts as the authorized dispenser
subtopic: Scope of the Medication Guide regulation and its definitions
rule_summary: Under 21 CFR 208.1(a), Part 208 sets forth requirements for patient labeling for human prescription drug products, including biological products, that FDA determines pose a serious and significant public health concern requiring distribution of FDA-approved patient information. It applies primarily to human prescription drug products used on an outpatient basis without direct supervision by a health professional, and it applies to new prescriptions and refill prescriptions. Under 208.1(b) the purpose of the patient labeling is to provide information when FDA determines in writing that it is necessary to patients' safe and effective use of drug products. Under 208.1(c) patient labeling will be required if FDA determines that one or more of three circumstances exists: the product is one for which patient labeling could help prevent serious adverse effects; the product has serious risk(s), relative to benefits, of which patients should be made aware because information concerning the risk(s) could affect patients' decision to use, or to continue to use, the product; or the product is important to health and patient adherence to directions for use is crucial to its effectiveness. Under 208.3, an authorized dispenser is an individual licensed, registered, or otherwise permitted by the jurisdiction in which the individual practices to provide drug products on prescription in the course of professional practice; a licensed practitioner is an individual so permitted to prescribe drug products; dispense to patients means the act of delivering a prescription drug product to a patient or an agent of the patient either by a licensed practitioner or an agent of a licensed practitioner, directly or indirectly, for self-administration by the patient, or the patient's agent, or outside the licensed practitioner's direct supervision, or by an authorized dispenser or an agent of an authorized dispenser under a lawful prescription of a licensed practitioner; distribute means delivering a drug product, other than by dispensing, to any person; a patient is any individual with respect to whom a drug product is intended to be, or has been, used; and a Medication Guide is FDA-approved patient labeling conforming to the specifications set forth in Part 208 and other applicable regulations.
exam_relevance: Fixes two facts that decide counter questions: Part 208 applies to refill prescriptions as well as new ones, and its dispensing duty is framed around an individual authorized dispenser whose agent may carry out the delivery.

Medication Guides for Prescription Drug Products: definitions

exceptions: Part 208 applies primarily, not exclusively, to products used on an outpatient basis without direct supervision by a health professional.
common_confusions: Treating the Medication Guide as owed only on a new prescription; 21 CFR 208.1(a) applies Part 208 to refill prescriptions as well.

Reading the authorized dispenser as the pharmacy business; 21 CFR 208.3(a) defines an individual permitted by the jurisdiction to provide drug products on prescription in the course of professional practice.
Assuming every prescription drug carries a Medication Guide; patient labeling under Part 208 is required when FDA determines that one of the circumstances in 21 CFR 208.1(c) exists.
verification_notes: Read the current text of 21 CFR 208.1 and 208.3 on eCFR on 2026-09-14. The eCFR version history for Part 208 shows its latest amendment dated 2016-11-29.
